# Plan: fast-serve on Rspack (branch `rspack`)

Goal: the same product as the Vite version (branch `v1.24`, `1.24.0-beta.3`): a zero-config `fast-serve` CLI replacing `heft start` for SPFx 1.24.x, serving web parts, extensions and ACEs on a real SharePoint page with HMR and React Fast Refresh, built on Rspack (`@rspack/core`, `@rspack/dev-server`, `@rspack/plugin-react-refresh`, `builtin:swc-loader`). Then compare it with Vite fast-serve and `heft start` (task R24; Vite `bundledDev` dropped from the comparison).

Binding: **our own Rspack config, written from scratch.** No heft webpack config, no `@microsoft/spfx-heft-plugins` internals (`WebpackConfigurationGenerator`, `ManifestPlugin`, `AsyncComponentPlugin`, `_LegacyExternals`…). Reading heft's sources and output to learn the expected format is fine. Public npm packages that SPFx projects already have (for example `@microsoft/sp-css-loader`, `@rushstack/heft-sass-plugin` for typings) may be loaded from the project, as the Vite version does.

Background: [prototype and numbers](README.md), [bundled-dev comparison](../bundled-dev/README.md), [HANDOFF](../HANDOFF.md). Reference implementation: `git show v1.24:src/...`, the v1.24 `kb/`, README and `research/`.

## Conventions

- Size: **S** ≤ ½ day, **M** ≈ 1 day, **L** ≈ 2 days of agent work (upper bound for one task).
- Status: ⬜ open · 🔄 in progress · ✅ done · ⏭️ not needed (reason in the row).
- Every task ends with `pnpm -s build && pnpm -s lint && pnpm -s typecheck && pnpm -s test` green, the version bumped to the next `1.24.0-rspack.<n>`, and the KB updated for what changed.
- "Integration test" = a vitest test running a real Rspack compile (or dev server) against a fake SPFx project in `test/fixtures/`. "Live" = the `spfx-debugging` skill on a copy of spfx-rea / spfx-bench in `/var/tmp/rspack-impl/`.
- Module layout as in the Vite version: `src/<feature>/index.ts` returns the feature's Rspack config contribution (rules, plugins, resolve, dev-server middlewares) plus its own runtime and tests; `project/` stays bundler-free.

## Architecture (target)

config (`fast-serve/config.json`, CLI flags, `config/serve.json`) → **project model** (plain Node: `config/config.json` bundles/components, source manifests, `serve.json` configurations, SPFx libraries in `node_modules`, `config.json` externals, loc files, tsconfig, `config/sass.json`, SPFx version) → **generated artifacts** (bundle entry modules, debug `manifests.js`, typings) → **Rspack compiler + `@rspack/dev-server`** (one compilation; one entry per SPFx bundle, AMD output, in-memory) → **browser runtime** (Rspack's HMR runtime and React Refresh inside each AMD bundle, plus small fast-serve runtimes: error forwarding).

Key differences from the Vite version, decided up front:
- SharePoint loads ordinary AMD bundles (`define([...externals], factory)`) like heft's, so no AMD shim, no ESM entry, no `/@spfx/` endpoints, no top-level-await facades.
- webpack semantics come for free: `require()`, UMD/AMD in dependencies, CommonJS interop, named imports from AMD externals as property reads at runtime, tolerance of type-only re-exports (`exportsPresence: 'auto'`).
- The cost moves from page load to start and edits: one full compile at start (spfx-bench ≈1.6 s), rebuild 0.1–0.3 s per edit (prototype numbers).

- Vite lessons: React stays the project's development copy (Fast Refresh); DefinePlugin values as in `transforms/defines.ts`.
- Prototype lessons: Rspack 2 panics on `md5`; `library.type` (not `libraryTarget`); externals need `externalsType: 'amd'` or they become `module.exports = …`; `exportsPresence` defaults to `error` in Rspack 2 → `auto`.

Pulled forward because spfx-rea can't compile without them: `localizedResources` bundled through `resolve.alias` to the model's strings file (locale + `en-us` fallback; rest in R10), images/fonts as `asset/resource` like heft's list (R12 verifies), basic styles: `sass-loader` (project `sass-embedded`/`sass`, `modern-compiler`, `silenceDeprecations`, `NodePackageImporter`) → project `@microsoft/sp-css-loader` (heft's rules for `.module(.scss).css` and global `.css`). - Done (`1.24.0-rspack.3`): `@rspack/dev-server` (HTTPS, dev certificate, `host: 'localhost'`, `static: false`, in-memory output, `devMiddleware.publicPath: '/dist/'`, `stats: 'none'`, `setupExitSignals: false`, compression off), CORS/PNA via `headers` + an `OPTIONS` → 204 middleware, our `manifests.js` (rendered per request, `no-store`, waits for the first compile), relative manifest icons served from their source files, 404 for everything else; ready banner and debug URL ported; compile lines `compiled/rebuilt in … ms: n errors, m warnings`; SIGINT/SIGTERM stop the server and close the compiler (idempotent). Feature contributions can now add dev-server middlewares. Decisions: `scriptResources` per bundle = the SPFx libraries among the external modules of the entry's chunks and their async chunks (collected on every `done`) + `@microsoft/sp-loader`, like heft; `allowedHosts: 'all'` like heft (otherwise `@rspack/dev-server` answers SharePoint's cross-site `no-cors` script requests with 403 and closes the websocket for the tenant origin); the port is checked on 127.0.0.1 and ::1 before start because the dev server throws listen errors as uncaught exceptions; `hot` + `liveReload` on with client `logging: 'warn'` and the compile-error overlay per `--no-overlay` (polish in R5/R14); `compileOnce` stays for tests. Left: HMR/Fast Refresh and several bundles per page (R5), terminal formatting/overlay filter (R14), project-change restarts (R17), deep library imports in `scriptResources` (R8), `config.json` externals (R9).

**R5 HMR and Fast Refresh.** `hot: true`, client `webSocketURL` `wss://localhost:<port>`, `@rspack/plugin-react-refresh` (SWC `react.refresh` + `development`, `overlay: false`, refresh only for `src`), React/react-dom/`react/jsx-runtime`/`react-dom/client` aliased to the project's copy (nested React copies, e.g. PnP's React 17, collapse), updates reaching the bundle entry (component class) → full page reload, several bundles on one page each with its own hot-update global (prototype `PerRuntimeHotUpdateGlobalPlugin`, or a `MultiCompiler` with one `uniqueName` per bundle; decide here by a short measurement: rebuild time, memory, complexity).
- Vite lessons: one tab only while checking HMR; HMR-boundary rules (mixed exports, services, ACE views) are the same, documented later; React 18 reports a render error 2–3 times.
- Prototype lessons: shared `uniqueName` → second bundle silently swallows every update; nested React 17 → "Invalid hook call".
- Acceptance: integration test with two bundles asserting distinct hot-update globals in the emitted runtime; **live:** spfx-rea TSX edit keeps SecondWebPart's counter (3/3), web part class edit reloads; spfx-bench edits in both bundles hot-update (BenchTree and BenchPnp).
- Done (`1.24.0-rspack.4`): new `hmr` feature: `@rspack/plugin-react-refresh` (loader limited to the project's `src`, its own entry replaced) + SWC `react.refresh`, fast-serve's refresh entry as a global entry (injects the refresh runtime into React's DevTools hook **per bundle**: the plugin's entry guards injection with a window flag named after `uniqueName`, so with several bundles only the first would get Fast Refresh), and a runtime-module plugin that fans the shared hot-update global out to every bundle's runtime (Rspack's handler ignores chunk ids it didn't request; also covers async chunks shared by bundles). **Decision: one compilation, not `MultiCompiler`** (measured with `research/rspack/scripts/measure-hmr-variants.mjs`, watch mode + HMR plugin, 2 runs each): spfx-rea (5 bundles) first compile 0.56 vs 0.58–0.60 s, RSS equal (0.28–0.29 GB after 8 edits), rebuild 65–124 vs 16–57 ms; spfx-bench (2 bundles) 1.55–1.58 vs 1.63–1.66 s, 0.54 vs 0.52–0.53 GB, rebuild 79–228 vs 80–147 ms; bench with every bundle ×5 (10 bundles sharing modules) 1.7–1.9 vs 5.1–5.3 s and 0.70–0.75 vs 1.0 GB, rebuild 250–470 vs 230–320 ms. MultiCompiler's faster rebuilds don't outweigh start/memory growth with shared dependencies plus per-compiler plugins/merged stats. Styles: a small loader after `sp-css-loader` routes `loadStyles` through a hot-styles runtime: first evaluation keeps load-themed-styles' batched insertion (per-module elements cost 0.2–0.4 s per F5 on spfx-bench), hot re-evaluations insert their own element and remove it on the next dispose, so `<style>` elements don't pile up (at most the inert original batch + the current one; class names change with content). Hot-update files `no-store` (dev-server `headers` function); browser console silent (client logging `warn`). Browser runtimes compiled by a separate `tsconfig.runtime.json` (ES2020, DOM) into `lib/`. Verified: integration test with a real dev server and both fixture bundles evaluated in one fake page (fake RequireJS/script loading, real websocket and fetch): component edits in each bundle apply without reload, style edits don't pile up, hot-update files `no-store`, class edit reloads, empty console; it fails for the first bundle without the fan-out (checked); unit tests for the fan-out, the hot-styles loader/runtime and headers. **Live** (fresh tarball, headless Chrome, visible tab): spfx-rea Second TSX edit keeps the counter (3 clicks → "Clicked 3 times" across 3/3 edits), save → DOM 117–163 ms (11 runs), HelloWorld TSX 130–150 ms, HelloWorld SCSS 119–174 ms without reload and with a constant number of style elements, `HelloWorldWebPart.ts`/`SecondWebPart.ts` edits reload (counter reset); HelloWorld and Second are one bundle in spfx-rea, so the several-bundle case was checked on spfx-bench: tree leaf TSX 156–225 ms, mid TSX 173–220 ms, SCSS 173–229 ms (style count constant), BenchPnp TSX 180–284 ms with loaded PnP data kept; RSS spfx-rea 0.25 GB ready / 0.30 GB after edits, spfx-bench 0.55–0.60 GB during edits; F5 spfx-bench 2.6–2.8 s. Found while measuring: a hidden tab (another tab restored from the Chrome profile) throttles timers to 1 s and delays Fast Refresh, now in the skill's checks. Left: one compile-error overlay per bundle with several bundles (R14), ACE/extension edits (R6/R7), class-name parity (R11).

**R8 SPFx libraries as AMD externals.** Every package with an SPFx library manifest (not only `@microsoft/sp-*`), plus `@microsoft/microsoft-graph-client` (in the model since R2, heft's non-standard external), and its known deep entry points as externals by exact request; manifest `scriptResources` with the library's id and version; libraries used only from async chunks still listed; React and react-dom deliberately bundled (development build), `react-dom/server` etc. resolved from the project.
- Vite lessons: the library detection of `project/libraries.ts` is reused. **Not needed with Rspack:** on-demand TLA facades, sync facades + per-chunk preload, facades in pre-bundling, export-name probing, `@microsoft/sp-lodash-subset` evaluation — webpack AMD externals import the module object and read names at use, like heft.
- Acceptance: integration test: imports of named, namespace and default exports from a library compile to property reads on the AMD dependency; manifest lists the right ids/versions; **live:** spfx-bench (PnP controls, `@pnp/sp`, Fluent) renders with the tenant's libraries (tenant 1.25 vs project 1.24.1 is fine).
- Done (`1.24.0-rspack.6`, together with R9/R10): externals = every SPFx library of the model + `config.json` externals, by exact request (as since R3). **Deep imports decision:** bundled from `node_modules` like heft (heft's externals are exact strings), with a one-time warning per request (`finishModules` scan for files inside a library package reached by a `<library>/…` request); the deep file's own library imports stay externals and are listed. First implemented as "deep import → external of the library root" (an externals function): live, a deep *default* import (`@microsoft/sp-core-library/lib/Version`) became `undefined`, because the root doesn't re-export everything; reverted. New: a rebuild that changes any bundle's external list (new library/external import) **reloads the page** — a hot update cannot add an AMD external (the update threw "`__rspack_external__microsoft_sp_http` is not defined" and React Refresh left a broken component). Reload is sent through the dev server (`static-changed`) from a `done` tap that runs before the dev server announces the update, so the broken update is never applied (live: no console error). Feature contributions can now register a `serverStarted` hook (page reloader). Verified: integration test on the new `test/fixtures/externals` (real dev server + fake RequireJS page): define list (`@contoso/spfx-lib` used only in a lazy chunk, `sp-core-library` from inside the bundled deep file, used externals), library code not bundled, manifest resources incl. a third-party library, lazy chunk gets the page's library, deep import bundled (named + default) with the warning, reload on adding an import (fails without the reload, checked). **Live:** spfx-bench (fresh tarball, port 4432): both web parts render (tree, PnP PeoplePicker/ListView with `@pnp/sp` call), 0 console errors, compile 1.6 s; spfx-rea: deep default import hot-updated, adding `@microsoft/sp-http` and `@microsoft/sp-http-base` imports reloaded and rendered. Manifests vs heft's `dist/` (both projects): same libraries and versions; differences only `@microsoft/sp-loader` (ours, like heft's `manifests.js`) and the known ACE async-loader difference.

**R9 `config.json` externals.** Entries `{ path, globalName?, globalDependencies? }` or URL strings → AMD externals; manifest `scriptResources` `{ type: 'path', path, globalName?, globalDependencies? }` like heft (URLs as is, local files served under `/dist/`); non-AMD scripts via `globalName` shim by sp-loader. Validation warnings (missing file, bad shape).
- Vite lessons: port `project/configExternals.ts` (validation); the webpack-like import semantics the Vite version emulated (`externals/externalImports.ts`) are native here (**not needed**); `export * from '<external>'` probably works under webpack (dynamic re-export) — verify instead of warning. CDN externals need the tenant's CSP to allow the host (heft limitation too).
- Acceptance: integration test with a local-file external and a URL external (manifest shape, AMD deps); **live:** one `config.json` external (e.g. a local UMD file) loads on the page, named import works.
- Done (`1.24.0-rspack.6`): manifest entries like heft's `LegacyExternals`: `{ type: 'path', path, globalName?, globalDependencies? }` only for bundles that import the external, plus its global dependencies (transitively); URL as is, local file as relative `<name><ext>` (heft's serve-mode name) emitted as an in-memory asset under `/dist/` (CORS headers as for bundles). Local files are watched: an edit **reloads the page** (no module changes, so the HMR client alone would do nothing). webpack semantics verified, nothing emulated: named import read at use, `import * as`/`require` = raw module (a function stays callable), default import = the module for a `globalName` shim, `export { x } from`, `export * as`, and **`export * from '<external>'` works** (names copied at runtime; the Vite version warned). Verified: integration test (URL, local file with `globalName`, local file with a local global dependency, unused external not listed, served file contents, every import form, reload on a local-file edit — fails without the reload, checked); bundler-free validation tests ported in R2. **Live** (spfx-rea copy, port 4431; CDNs blocked by the tenant CSP, so local copies): ejs 3.1.8 `render` named import, apexcharts 3.42 AMD build with `globalName` as default import (`function`), a non-AMD global with a global dependency → web part showed `ejs: Contoso; apexcharts: function; legacy: legacy global from Contoso`, requests `/dist/ejs.js`, `/dist/apexcharts.js`, `/dist/contoso-legacy.js`, `/dist/contoso-legacy-dep.js`; editing the legacy file reloaded with the new text.
- For R17: local-file externals are in the model's watched files (`invalidate` → `model`); they are now handled live (asset + reload), so a restart is not needed for their edits.

- Acceptance: integration test with AMD and TS loc files, `--locale de-de` and fallback; **live:** spfx-rea strings render, a string edit updates.
- Done (`1.24.0-rspack.6`): loc format decided from the file text at start (`define(` outside comments → AMD, aliased directly; otherwise aliased to a virtual CommonJS wrapper exporting the module's default export or the module, so `import * as strings` works for `export default`/`export =`/`module.exports` files, as the Vite version did) with the Vite version's heft warning, once per resource. String edits: loc used only by components → hot update; loc imported by the class → reload (normal HMR bubbling, nothing loc-specific). **R11 Sass, CSS modules, theme tokens.** `sass-loader` (`api: 'modern-compiler'`) with the project's Sass implementation (`sass-embedded`, else `sass`), `silenceDeprecations` from the merged `config/sass.json` (only that field; edit → restart in R17), `pkg:` URLs through Sass's `NodePackageImporter`, `~` imports (sass-loader handles them), CSS modules with SPFx class names (`<local>_<hash>`) and theme tokens (`"[theme:x, default:y]"`) resolved at runtime through `@microsoft/load-themed-styles`. Global `.scss`, plain `.css`, library `.module.scss.css` (PnP) through the same rules. CSS HMR: style module re-evaluates, component re-renders (old `<style>` may stay; check that it does not break visuals).
- Vite lessons: `styles/sassOptions.ts` (`NodePackageImporter` from the Sass package actually used, `pkg:` difference to heft documented), partials must never be compiled as roots (warmup bug), theme tokens resolve once per insert (no theme-change monitoring), `@pnp/spfx-property-controls` 3.13 CSS cut stays cut.

Verified: integration tests (fixture compiled by heft's own `SassProcessor` → our class names equal heft's for `.module.scss` with `pkg:`/`~`/`@use` and `.module.sass`; tokens kept; global/library CSS and `url()` asset; deprecation warning without silence, none with; `loadPaths`). Live (spfx-rea copy, port 4431): startup 0 warnings (rig silences `import`), all 8 class names in the served bundles equal heft's algorithm on the copy's `lib/` (spfx-bench copy: 484/484, 0 warnings), Fluent `$ms-font-size-xl` via `@import 'pkg:@fluentui/react/dist/sass/References.scss'` and a `~@fluentui/react/dist/sass/...` import rendered (21 px), theme token resolved to the site's `#8764b8`, an SCSS edit (new class, new property, swapped `~` import to `themeOverrides`) hot-updated without reload (rebuild 100–180 ms, one style element added). Note: Fluent's `References.scss` variables are static colours; themed tokens come from its `themeOverrides` partial (as with heft).

**R13 tsconfig.** `paths`/`baseUrl` (try Rspack `resolve.tsConfig` first; the Vite version needed its own resolver because a rig-extended `include` broke Vite's — if Rspack has the same gap, port `aliases/` as a resolver plugin or `resolve.alias` from the model), SWC options from tsconfig: `experimentalDecorators` → `legacyDecorator`, `emitDecoratorMetadata` → `decoratorMetadata`, `useDefineForClassFields`, target, JSX; `const enum`: per-file limit same as Oxc → keep the clear error/warning (port `transforms/constEnums` as a loader-agnostic check or warning on the compile error); type-only re-exports: `exportsPresence: 'auto'` + filter the "export … was not found" warnings like heft (**Vite's `typeOnlyNames` guard not needed**, SWC emits `typeof X === "undefined" ? Object : X` for decorator metadata like `tsc`). tsconfig change → restart (R17).

Type-only names: no Vite-style guard; `exportsPresence: 'auto'` makes them harmless, and the "export 'X' … was not found" warnings are dropped only when both modules are project files and the target declares `X` only as `interface`/`type` (other missing exports keep the warning; `typeof X` uses never warn). `const enum`: project `export const enum` works; ported the two v1.24 checks that still add value: a global `declare const enum` from a project `.d.ts` used as a value → compile error (post-loader on SWC output, `.d.ts` rescanned per rebuild); an import of a `.d.ts`-only module → Rspack's "Module not found" replaced by the explanation (afterSeal). Dependency `const enum`s keep Rspack's warning (documented). Verified: integration tests (all decorator kinds + metadata, field without initializer under ES5/ES2022, alias through rig extends, type-only re-export and metadata imports without warnings, a real missing export still warned, both const-enum errors) and unit tests; live: a `paths` alias import and a legacy-decorated class rendered on the page.

**R14 Error overlay and terminal noise.** Rspack's client overlay for compile errors (`overlay: { errors: true, warnings: false }`), runtime errors in the overlay only for project code (the client's `runtimeErrors` filter function: project frames, not SharePoint's own errors), `--no-overlay` / `"overlay": false`; terminal: concise compile results (`errors` with file:line and code frame, warnings deduplicated, Sass deprecations silenced per `sass.json`), `infrastructureLogging` quiet, no dev-server banners, browser console logging `warn` (no `[HMR] Waiting for update signal…` noise).
- Vite lessons: overlay over SharePoint pages works; an overlay during page load → first edit reloads (check Rspack's behaviour); React reports render errors 2–3× → signature filter. **Not needed:** hiding Node's HTTP/2 status-message warning (`@rspack/dev-server` serves HTTPS over HTTP/1.1; the Chrome HTTP/2 stall is gone with it), Vite overlay-text hint.
- Acceptance: unit tests for the filter and terminal formatting; **live:** syntax error → overlay over the page, cleared after the fix; a thrown error in a component → overlay; SharePoint's own errors → no overlay.
- Done (`1.24.0-rspack.8`, together with R15): **the dev server's own overlay is off; fast-serve draws one overlay per page from a page runtime inlined at the top of `manifests.js`** (runs once per page before any bundle, keyed by origin). Reason: every bundle carries its own dev-server client, and SharePoint re-evaluates a bundle whose AMD factory throws (3 evaluations seen for one bundle with a syntax error) → Rspack's overlay showed 3 stacked iframes live. The runtime listens to the `webpackErrors`/`webpackInvalid`/`webpackOk`/`webpackStillOk` window messages every client posts (same text the client logs) and renders one overlay in a shadow root (Esc/×/backdrop close; closes on the next rebuild; runtime errors never replace a shown compile error; `overlay: false`/`--no-overlay` turns both off). Terminal: compile problems as `error in <project-relative path>[:loc]` + Rspack's message with the "Module build failed (from …)" wrapper unwrapped and dedented, duplicates dropped; summary `compiled in N ms` / `rebuilt in N ms (<changed files, max 2 +n more>)` with `: 1 error, 2 warnings` only when non-zero; no dev-server/Rspack noise found to filter (`infrastructureLogging: warn`, `stats: 'none'`, client logging `warn`; nothing printed on start, connect or SIGINT). Verified: unit tests (formatting, location from module identifier, dedupe, summary), integration test with a real dev server and both fixture bundles in one fake page: a syntax error → one overlay, project path in the terminal, rebuild line with `1 error`, fix → overlay closed and clean rebuild line. **Live** (spfx-rea copy, port 4431): syntax error during a session → one overlay, cleared after the fix without reload; syntax error at page load (bundle evaluated 3×) → 1 overlay (was 3 with Rspack's overlay); spfx-bench copy (two bundles on one page, port 4432): one overlay, cleared after the fix; SharePoint's own console errors → no overlay, nothing in the terminal.

**R15 Browser errors in the terminal, readable load errors.** A small runtime in each bundle (added as an entry) reports uncaught errors/rejections and `console.error` with a project frame to the server (`POST /@fast-serve/browser-errors` or the dev-server websocket if extensible), source-mapped with a code frame in the terminal; readable message when a bundle fails to load or a component export is missing (SharePoint otherwise shows `[object Object]`), e.g. via a wrapper in the entry; "server error" status so the page reloads after a fix.
- Vite lessons: port the frame rule, formatting and source-map logic of `browserErrors/`; only project code is forwarded. The AMD "Mismatched anonymous define()" hint is likely **not needed** (R16).
- Acceptance: unit tests; **live:** an error in a component's render shows in the terminal once with the right file:line.
- Done (`1.24.0-rspack.8`): the same page runtime wraps `console.error` and listens to `error`/`unhandledrejection`; it POSTs to `https://localhost:<port>/fast-serve/browser-errors` (`text/plain`, CORS) only reports whose stack mentions `https://localhost:<port>/dist/`, each error object once (claimed only when actually sent), skipping `[rspack-dev-server]`/`[HMR]`/`[fast-serve]` console lines. Server: frames in served files are mapped through the bundle's `.map` from the dev server's in-memory output (also hot-update files; cache dropped per compile); a frame is a project frame when it maps to an existing file in the project outside `node_modules`; only reports with a project frame are printed (stack trimmed after the last project frame, code frame, `file:line` — `cheap-module-source-map` has no columns, so no column/caret), repeated signatures within 2 s suppressed (React replays); the response carries overlay content for uncaught errors/rejections (not `console.error`). **Load errors:** SharePoint logs `Could not load <bundle> in require.` with the RequireJS error and its web part box shows `ERROR:[object Object]`; the runtime reports it as `load-error` (bundle known from the page config), the server explains it (`scripterror` of a `config.json` external → name + URL/path; of an SPFx library → package/id/version; factory threw while the compile has errors or with "Module build failed" → compile error; otherwise the thrown error with mapped frames) and answers with a page message that replaces `[object Object]` in the bundle's web part error boxes (60 s observer, as in v1.24); after a load failure the page reloads on the first `webpackOk` that follows a `webpackInvalid`. Hints that still apply: only those (the AMD-mismatch, `const enum`/missing-export and computed-`require` hints of v1.24 have no Rspack counterpart). Verified: unit tests (frames, source-name resolution, formatting, load-error reasons, report parsing, reporter filter/repeat/overlay option with a real SWC source map, dependency frames inside the project's `node_modules` not counted), page-runtime tests in a fake page (forwarding filter, once per object, console call sites, singleton, load error + readable error box, one overlay for several clients, runtime overlay vs compile overlay, overlay off, reload after failure), integration test (an error thrown from a component in a real bundle → `src/…/First.tsx:6` with code frame, printed once, overlay; non-project report ignored). **Live** (spfx-rea copy): throw in an `onClick` → terminal `[Unhandled error] Error: r14 click boom` `> onClick src/webparts/second/components/Second.tsx:12` with code frame + overlay; throw in render after an edit → printed once (`Second.tsx:9`); syntax error at page load → error boxes show `[fast-serve] bundle "hello-world-web-part" could not be loaded: a module in it failed to compile; the page reloads after the fix…`, the fix reloaded the page and it rendered; a `config.json` external pointing at a missing URL → terminal and both error boxes name the external and its URL.

**R16 Bare `require()` and AMD isolation.** Expected **not needed** as features: webpack resolves `require('<literal>')` at build time (CommonJS `module.exports`, ESM namespace, JSON, assets), and its parser handles `define`/UMD in dependencies itself, so the page's RequireJS never sees them (lodash's AMD branch sets `window._` exactly like heft). Task = regression tests only, plus documenting `amdPackages` as dropped.
- From R3: Rspack 2 parses AMD only when `amd` is set; the config sets `amd: {}` (webpack default behaviour). The regression tests must cover it.
- Acceptance: integration tests: `require` of a CommonJS package, an ESM package, JSON and an asset from `src`; a UMD dependency with an AMD branch and the full `lodash` build compile and run in a fake RequireJS page (no "Mismatched anonymous define()").
- Done (`1.24.0-rspack.8`): regression tests only, nothing to implement. One compile of a fixture whose web part `require`s a CommonJS package (`module.exports`, function kept callable), an ES module package (namespace), a side-effect-only package, JSON (parsed), a PNG (dev-server URL), a UMD package that checks AMD first (AMD branch runs against webpack's `define`), the full `lodash` build (works, `import * as` and `require` agree, `window._` set like heft), `@microsoft/sp-core-library` and a CommonJS dependency that `require`s an SPFx library and a `config.json` external (both stay AMD externals on the bundle's `define`, identical objects); evaluated with a page `define` that has `define.amd` and throws "Mismatched anonymous define() module" on a second call: called exactly once. With `amd: false` the suite fails (checked), so it guards the `amd: {}` setting. `require()` rewriting, AMD isolation, `amdPackages` and the mismatch hint stay ⏭️ (`amdPackages` is ignored with a warning since R1). **Live** (spfx-rea copy): `import { chunk, VERSION } from 'lodash'` in a component rendered `lodash 4.18.1: [[1,2],[3]]` with SharePoint's RequireJS on the page, `window._` is lodash, no console errors.

**R17 Options completion and restarts.** Final option set (`port`, `pageUrl`, `locale`, `serveConfiguration`, `overlay`; anything Rspack-specific decided in R21, e.g. persistent cache), dev session that restarts the compiler/server on edits of `config/config.json`, `config/serve.json` (URL), `config/sass.json`, tsconfig (transform options, `paths`), `fast-serve/config.json`, `package.json` dependency changes; new/deleted components picked up.
- Vite lessons: port `devSession.ts` (a failing restart keeps the old server or exits clearly); which edits reload vs restart.
- Acceptance: unit tests for the restart rules; integration test: edit `config/sass.json` → restart.
- Done (`1.24.0-rspack.9`, together with R18–R20): option set unchanged and final (`port`, `pageUrl`, `locale`, `serveConfiguration`, `overlay`; R21 added no Rspack-specific option, the extend file can set `cache`). New dev session above the dev server: restarts on content changes of `package.json`, `config/config.json`, `config/serve.json`, `config/sass.json`, `fast-serve/config.json`, the tsconfig chain, component manifests, extend-file candidates (add/remove) and the extend file's local imports; local-file `config.json` externals stay live (R9), new library/external imports keep the R8 reload. **Decision: always a full restart, no in-place recompile** — a new server starts in ~0.2 s on spfx-rea, and options, model and config are rebuilt consistently. The new options/model/extend/config/compiler are prepared while the old server runs; only then the old one closes and the new one listens on the (possibly new) port. A failing preparation (`config/config.json` unreadable, broken extend file, invalid config) prints `restart failed: …` / `<file> could not be loaded:` + "The server keeps running with the previous configuration; fast-serve restarts when the file is fixed."; only a listen failure after the swap exits 1. Watching: per folder (non-recursive, nearest existing parent for missing folders) with a content hash per file, 100 ms settle, one queued restart. Pages reload by themselves: every server start sets a new `output.hashSalt`, so reconnecting clients see a new hash, the hot check against the old one finds nothing and the page reloads (live, also when no module changed). Restart output: reason line, warnings, `Rspack config: …`, compile line, `restarted in N ms at …` (full banner only when port/page/serve configuration/components changed). Verified: watcher and restart-reason unit tests; session integration test (helper edit, broken + fixed extend, `config/sass.json`, broken + restored `config/config.json`, extend removal; bundle content and headers after each). **Live** (spfx-rea copy, port 4433): extend file added while running → restart; helper edit and extend edit → server restarted in 0.18–0.25 s, page reloaded by itself with the new values (≈4 s incl. SharePoint reload); `config/sass.json` edit restarted; TSX edit after restarts hot-updated with state kept; SIGINT stopped the server.

**R18 Extend file.** Optional `fast-serve/rspack.extend.mjs` (`.js`, `.cjs`; `.mts`/`.ts` only if Node's type stripping is available — decide), exporting a Rspack `Configuration` or `defineConfig((context) => Configuration)`, sync or async; merged under fast-serve's config (arrays appended: `plugins`, `module.rules`, `resolve.alias`, `externals`…), protected keys (`entry`, `output.*`, `devServer.server/port/host`, `externalsType`, `mode`…) warn and are ignored; context: `root`, `port`, `publicPath`, `locale`, `serveConfiguration`, `pageUrl`, `spfxVersion`, `fastServeVersion`, `rspackVersion`; edits of the file and its local imports restart; add/delete restarts; broken file at start stops with the file name, broken edit keeps the server. Public entry `exports["."]`: `defineConfig` + types (`FastServeConfig`, `FastServeContext`, Rspack's `Configuration`).
- Vite lessons: port the structure of `viteExtend/` (files, context, guard, watch) and `publicApi.test.ts`; webpack customizations are never run automatically. Much simpler translation story: most heft webpack customizations (`DefinePlugin`, aliases, rules) can be pasted with `rspack.*` equivalents.
- Acceptance: unit + integration tests (merge, guard warnings, restart on change, broken file); public `.d.ts` emitted.
- Done (`1.24.0-rspack.9`): `fast-serve/rspack.extend.mjs`, also `.mts`, `.js`, `.ts`, `.cjs`, `.cts` (first found wins, others warned). **Decision: `.mts`/`.ts` supported on Node 22.14** without Node type stripping: fast-serve bundles the file and its local imports with Rspack (`builtin:swc-loader` for TS, ES module output, bare imports external — `node-commonjs` for `require`, `module` for `import` — so `spfx-fast-serve-helpers`/`rspack` are fast-serve's instances) into a temporary `.mjs` next to it, imports and deletes it; a tiny loader declares `__dirname`/`__filename` per local module (Rspack's `node-module` mode would give the output folder); the compilation's file dependencies outside `node_modules` are the restart watch list; each load evaluates helpers afresh. Export: object, promise, or function `(context, env)`; `defineConfig` is an identity helper for types. Context: `root`, `port`, `origin`, `publicPath`, `locale`, `serveConfiguration`, `pageUrl`, `spfxVersion`, `fastServeVersion`, `rspackVersion` (frozen); env `{ command: 'serve', mode: 'development' }`. **R25 Overlay after the fix + npm peer conflict (user report on `1.24.0-rspack.11`).**
- Done (`1.24.0-rspack.12`): reproduced live on a spfx-rea copy: `React.useState1(…)`, `useState1(…)` with the import unchanged, and `import { useState1 } from 'react'` all reach the page as runtime errors (React is an external, so Rspack can't warn about the missing export; no type check in the dev loop); after the fix the build was green and Fast Refresh remounted the component, but the runtime-error overlay stayed (it was only closed by Esc/×). Also found: a rebuild with only warnings posts `webpackWarnings` instead of `webpackOk`, so it neither closed overlays nor triggered the reload after a load failure; the server's 2 s repeat suppression answered a repeated error without overlay content. Fix: the page runtime closes a runtime overlay on the first `webpackOk`/`webpackWarnings` after a `webpackInvalid` (not on a client's initial `ok`, not on `still-ok`), drops answers for reports sent before that update, does not redraw an identical overlay; the reload after a load failure also follows a warnings-only build (delayed 100 ms and cancelled when `webpackErrors` follows, because the dev server sends warnings before errors); the server returns the overlay for a repeated error and only skips the terminal print. Tests: 7 page-runtime/reporter unit tests and one dev-server integration test, all failing before the fix. Live (4435): all three variants + a still-broken edit (overlay re-opens, new element) + an `onClick` error with state kept (clicks preserved, overlay closed) + syntax error + a fix whose build has 1 warning: overlay closes in every case. npm: reproduced `ERESOLVE` (`css-loader` 7.1.2 exact or locked under `~7.1.2`, peer `@rspack/core@"0.x || 1.x"`); `css-loader` ≥ 7.1.4 accepts `^2.0.0-0`. No package-side fix: `@rspack/core` lands at the top of `node_modules`, `@rspack/dev-server` requires it as a peer (an aliased `@rspack/core` + dev-server probe package still fails with `ERESOLVE`), `overrides` are root-only, bundling would ship platform-specific native bindings. Documented: `npm install --save-dev css-loader@^7.1.4 <tgz>` (heft `npm run build` checked OK with 7.1.5) or `--legacy-peer-deps` / `.npmrc`.

**R27 Sass `~`/`pkg:` imports of exports-hidden files.**
- Done (`1.24.0-rspack.14`): `@import '~@microsoft/sp-office-ui-fabric-core/dist/sass/SPFabricCore.scss'` failed ("Can't find stylesheet to import"): sass-loader's resolver honours `exports`. `pkg:` of an exports-hidden path already worked through Sass's `NodePackageImporter` (it falls back to the package folder when `exports` has no match), but a `~` import inside the loaded file failed. Fix: a Sass `FileImporter` after `NodePackageImporter` (before sass-loader's importer) that handles `~x` and `pkg:x`: package folder from the importing file's folder upwards (real path), `exports` ignored, Sass tries partial/extensions/index itself; returned `file:` URLs end up in `loadedUrls`, so sass-loader adds them as dependencies. Found while verifying: heft's development webpack runs `source-map-loader` before `sp-css-loader`, which strips the `/*# sourceMappingURL */` line, so heft's development class names hash `css + "\n"`, not the lib file text; our mapper hashed the comment too (matched heft production / the lib algorithm only), so every class name differed from `heft start`'s. Changed to the development form; tests now compare with heft's `lib/` CSS after the same strip. Tests: integration (`~`/`pkg:` × `@import`/`@use` of an exports-hidden partial with a nested `~` into a package-local dependency, heft parity, file dependencies; all four failed before), unit tests for the importer. Local (spfx-rea copy, 4437): template line compiles, 9/9 class names equal heft's `heft build` (development) `dist/` bundles, typings byte-identical, edit rebuild 131 ms. Live: web part rendered with `fabricProbe_<hash>` equal to heft's, 21 px, theme primary colour. Vite `v1.24` (beta.3 tarball, copy, port 4438): same bug (`"./dist/sass/_SPFabricCore.scss" is not exported under the conditions ["sass", "style", "development", "import"]`); Vite 8 puts user importers before its internal one, so the same importer added after `NodePackageImporter` fixes it (checked by patching the copy's installed package): S, about 40 lines plus tests. The Vite line's class names are not heft's anyway (`[local]_[hash:base64:8]`).

## Vite-version items that are not needed with Rspack

| Vite item | Why not needed |
|---|---|
| AMD shim per bundle, ESM entry, `/@spfx/bundle`, `/@spfx/status` polling | SharePoint loads real AMD bundles; HMR runs inside them |
| on-demand TLA facades, CJS sync facades, per-chunk preload, facades in pre-bundling | AMD externals declared on the bundle's `define`, resolved by RequireJS before the bundle runs (like heft) |
| `externalImports` rewrite (named imports as property reads) | webpack's external module semantics already read properties at use |
| `require()` → import rewrite, scope analysis | webpack resolves `require` at build time |
| AMD isolation (`isolateAmd`), `amdPackages`, "Mismatched anonymous define" hint | webpack's parser handles `define` in dependencies; RequireJS never sees it (verified in R16) |
| type-only re-export guard (`typeOnlyNames`) | `exportsPresence: 'auto'` + warning filter, like heft |
| Vite CJS namespace-copy interop helper | webpack interop |
| library `.module.scss.css` via a separate compile path | the normal CSS rules apply (verify in R11) |
| pre-bundling, optimizer hash, warmup decisions | no pre-bundling; one compile at start |
| hidden HTTP/2 status-message warning | dev server uses HTTP/1.1 over TLS |
| Vite overlay-text hint | own overlay (page runtime in `manifests.js`) with fast-serve's own hint text |
